newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai sugar vessels movement slow this week.
newsitem.headline: Thai sugar vessels movement slow this week.

text.p: Thai sugar vessels movement continued to be slow with loading affected by rain and the season coming to an end, trade and shipping sources said on Thursday.
Only about 25,000 tonnes of sugar were shipped or scheduled to be shipped between September 24 and October 18, they said.
Vessel Yala Navee was scheduled to leave Thai port for Japan on October 7 with 17,650 tonnes of bagged white sugar.
Sangthai Ceramic left for Singapore on September 24 with 800 tonnes of bagged white sugar. Tate & Lyle was the buyer.
Tate & Lyle also bought 1,600 tonnes of white sugar to ship to South Korea, 1000 tonnes to Cambodia and another 1,000 tonnes to Singapore.

Vessel Dae Gak Bong was ready to leave Thai port for South Korea with the sugar on September 28. Sangthai Radium was scheduled to arrive for loading the sugar purchased by Tate & Lyle for Singapore between October 7-11.
Gill & Duffus was said to have bought 1,500 tonnes of white sugar to ship to Maldives. The vessel Sea Horse was scheduled to be ready on October 1.
